extracted.intended_audience: prospective commenters on land withdrawals; agency officials; investors and prospective buyers/ exporters of Commodity Credit Corporation (CCC) inventory; AID administrative officers
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register notices describing (1) procedures for proposed withdrawal and reservation of public lands (comment period, investigations, hearings, Secretary determination) and (2) Commodity Credit Corporation monthly sales program rules (availability, pricing formulas, offer/payment requirements, export controls, and related delegations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission period and method for comments on proposed withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: For a period of 30 days from the date of publication of this notice, all persons who wish to submit comments, suggestions, or objections in connection with the proposed withdrawal may present their views in writing to the undersigned officer of the Bureau of Land Management at the stated address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be written and mailed/received within 30 days to the specified Land Office Manager/office (316 North 26th Street, Billings, Mont. 59101).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized officer investigations under 43 CFR 2311.1-3(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorized officer of the Bureau of Land Management will undertake such investigations as are necessary to determine the existing and potential demand for the lands and their resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He will also negotiate with the applicant to adjust the application to: reduce the area to the minimum essential to meet applicant's needs; provide for maximum concurrent utilization for other purposes; eliminate lands needed for more essential purposes; and reach agreement on concurrent management of the lands and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report and Secretary determination for withdrawal application
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorized officer will prepare a report for consideration by the Secretary of the Interior who will determine whether or not the lands will be withdrawn as requested by the applicant agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary's determination will be published in the Federal Register; a separate notice will be sent to each interested party of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearing provision for withdrawal applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If circumstances warrant, a public hearing will be held at a convenient time and place, which will be announced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing is discretionary and will be announced separately when deemed warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redelegation of administrative authority (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Redelegations specify which authorities delegated to an Assistant Administrator are redelegated (to Deputy Assistant Administrator, Executive Director, Managing Director, Directors, Chiefs, etc.), the scope, and effective date; prior redelegations may be revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The redelegation text lists specific delegations (by number) and includes effective dates and confirmations of actions signed between given dates; it may also expressly revoke prior redelegations (e.g., redelegation dated April 1, 1966 revoked).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-redelegation rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority delegated in the redelegation may not be redelegated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The redelegation includes an explicit prohibition against further redelegation of the authorities granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing Director authority on investment guaranties (up to $5 million)
rubrics_metrics.description: To authorize, issue, and amend investment guaranties under section 221(b)(1) of the Foreign Assistance Act covering investments which take the form of royalties or which, as described in the Special Terms, do not exceed $5 million; and to make related approvals and determinations under sections 221(a), 221(b), 221(c), and 222(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority includes making the statutory approvals and determinations called for in the cited sections when guaranties meet the form/size criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing Director participation in financing surveys (section 231)
rubrics_metrics.description: To participate in financing surveys of investment opportunities under section 231 of the Foreign Assistance Act and make the determinations and exercise the functions provided for in that section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation authority is coupled with making required determinations under 22 U.S.C. §2191.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director, Insurance Division guaranty authority (up to $500,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: To authorize, issue, and amend investment guaranties under section 221(b)(1) covering investments which take the form of royalties or which do not exceed $500,000, and to make related approvals and determinations under sections 221(a), 221(b), 221(c), and 222(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may amend such guaranties provided amendments do not increase the amount covered; related authorities limited by monetary cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director, Insurance Division participation in financing surveys (up to $5,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: To participate, in an amount not to exceed $5,000, in financing surveys of investment opportunities under section 231 and to make the determinations and exercise the functions provided in that section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to investment surveys are permitted provided they do not increase AID's participation above $5,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Director authority on survey timing and contract assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: To extend the time provided in an investment survey in which a decision to invest may be made and to consent to assignments of any contract of guaranty issued under section 221(b)(1) under specified statutory assignment provisions, provided such assignments run to entities eligible to be issued investment guaranties under the then-applicable legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consents to assignment are constrained by eligibility of assignees under the governing statutes (Mutual Security Act, Economic Cooperation Act, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delinquency notice and cancellation authority
rubrics_metrics.description: To issue written notice of delinquency to any investor who has failed to pay any fee due under any contract of guaranty issued under section 221(b)(1) or related statutes, and to cancel any contract of guaranty when the investor fails to pay the delinquent fee within thirty (30) days following written notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority delegated concurrently to Associate Director, Insurance Division and Chief, International Loan Branch, Accounting Division; cancellation triggers after 30 days nonpayment post-notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to modify reporting requirements in guaranties and surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Chief, Administration Branch, Finance Division authorized to amend investment guaranties and investment surveys to modify the reporting requirements thereunder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments limited to reporting requirements; redelegation effective June 4, 1967, and supersedes prior delegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation of actions signed before redelegation effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: Investment guaranties, investment surveys, and amendments to either, signed between June 4, 1967 and the effective date of this redelegation by certain named signatories are confirmed to have been signed with authority delegated to those signatories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The redelegation explicitly confirms prior acts by named individuals as having been within delegated authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCC Monthly Sales List purpose and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The CCC Monthly Sales List identifies commodities available for sale (and for redemption of payment-in-kind certificates) and is designed to aid in moving CCC inventories into domestic or export use through regular commercial channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List varies month-to-month; announcements cited contain full sale terms and conditions; list is subject to amendment and such amendments will be furnished to persons receiving the list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commodities available and eligibility for sale
rubrics_metrics.description: CCC lists specific commodities available for sale (cotton, wheat, corn, oats, barley, rye, rice, grain sorghum, peanuts, flax, tung oil, butter, cheese, nonfat dry milk, etc.) and designates which may be sold for unrestricted use, export, or restricted purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CCC reserves right to determine class, grade, quality, and available quantity of listed commodities and to define or limit export areas prior to sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing general rule — storable vs nonstorable and minimums
rubrics_metrics.description: For many commodities, storable lots will be sold at market price as determined by CCC but not less than a specified percentage of the 1967 price-support loan rate (often 115%), plus applicable markups; nonstorable lots sold at not less than market price as determined by CCC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Export sales are frequently made at the higher of the domestic market price (as determined by CCC) or 115% of the applicable 1967 price-support loan rate plus carrying charges; statutory minimum for export price adjustments often referenced as 105% of loan rate plus markup. Specific markups and examples are provided for each commodity and type of carrier (truck, rail/barge, terminal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commodity-specific pricing and markup formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific commodities (wheat, corn, grain sorghum, oats, barley, rye, rice, cotton — upland and extra long staple, peanuts, etc.) have detailed pricing formulas, markups by carrier, and examples of minimum prices reflecting local/grade adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice contains tables/examples (dollars per bushel/in-store, by location and class) and specific announcement references (e.g., GR-346, GR-345, GR-261, GR-262, NO-C-32) governing sale method and pricing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offers and terms of sale (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCC will entertain offers from responsible buyers; offers accepted will be subject to terms prescribed by the Corporation, including payment by cash or irrevocable letter of credit before delivery, and removal of the commodity from CCC stocks within a reasonable period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where sales are for export, proof of exportation is required; buyer responsible for obtaining any required U.S. Government export permit or license; purchase does not guarantee such permits will be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial responsibility of offerer and security requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CCC reserves right to refuse to consider an offer if it does not have adequate information of the financial responsibility of the offerer. Offerer should submit a financial statement or consult the office; when satisfactory responsibility not established CCC may consider offer only upon submission of certified/cashier's check, a bid bond, or other security acceptable to CCC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security ensures compliance with payment and performance obligations if offer accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to reject or refuse offers and to amend announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: CCC reserves the right to reject any or all offers and to amend announcements from time to time; such amendments apply to and become part of sale contracts thereafter entered into.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material amendments (e.g., adding or removing a commodity or changing price/method of sale) will be announced to all persons currently receiving the list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for buyers on export sales (business presence and agent for service)
rubrics_metrics.description: On sales for which proof of export is required, the buyer shall be regularly engaged in the business of buying or selling commodities, maintain a bona fide business office in the United States (or territories/possessions), and have a person (principal or resident agent) upon whom service of judicial process may be had.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a condition for being eligible to purchase for export where proof must be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export prohibitions and license requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of Commerce regulations prohibit exportation or reexportation of any commodities under this program to Cuba, the Soviet Bloc, or Communist-controlled areas of the Far East (including Communist China, North Korea, and the Communist-controlled area of Viet Nam) except under a validated license issued by the Bureau of International Commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exporters must consult Commerce Department regulations and field offices for details and any changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Destination control statement requirement for exports
rubrics_metrics.description: For all exportations, one of the destination control statements specified in Commerce Department Regulations (§ 379.10(c)) is required to be placed on all copies of the shipper’s export declaration, all copies of the bill of lading, and all copies of the commercial invoices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exporter should communicate with the Bureau of International Commerce or its field offices to determine which statement to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCC Export Credit Sales Program interest rates and eligible commodities
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest rates per annum for January 1968 under the CCC Export Credit Sales Program were 6 percent for U.S. bank obligations and 7 percent for foreign bank obligations. Commodities eligible for financing include wheat, wheat flour, barley, bulgur, corn, cormeal, grain sorghum, upland and extra long staple cotton, tobacco, cottonseed oil, soybean oil, dairy products, tallow and beef breeding cattle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commodities purchased from CCC may be financed for export as private stocks under Announcement GSM-4; additional eligibility references provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redemption and special application sales (payment-in-kind, barter, barter contract conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain dispositions are tied to redemption of domestic payment-in-kind certificates or application to barter contracts; some commodities are available for barter contracts (e.g., oats, cotton, tobacco) and wheat/grain sorghum may be subject to special barter/export conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific announcements (e.g., GR-212, GR-261, GR-262, GR-345, GR-368, PS-1/PS-2/PS-3) set terms for these transactions and geographic/export constraints (e.g., west coast port restrictions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely small-lot disposals handled by ASCS offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Disposals and other handling of inventory items often result in small quantities at given locations or in qualities not up to specifications; these lots are offered by the appropriate ASCS office promptly upon appearance and generally do not appear in the Monthly Sales List.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Buyers should contact local ASCS offices or check weekly lot lists/invitations to bid for such lots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wheat export sale procedural requirements (notice and geographic limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain export programs, notice of foreign sale must be furnished to CCC within 5 calendar days after purchase and sales will be made only to fill dollar market sales abroad; exporter must show export from specified west coast geographic bounds (west of 170th meridian W and east of 60th meridian E) and to specified destination regions (west coast of Central and South America).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These geographic and timing constraints are tied to specific announcements (e.g., GR-345, GR-261) and apply to filling dollar-market sales abroad and barter contract conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cotton sale price floors and competitive offer rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Upland cotton is sold by competitive offers under Announcement NO-C-32 (unrestricted use) and NO-C-31 (redemption/ barters etc.), at the highest price offered but not less than the higher of (a) 110 percent of the current loan rate for such cotton, or (b) the market price as determined by CCC. Extra long staple cotton sold at highest offer but not less than higher of (a) 115 percent of current support price plus reasonable carrying charges, or (b) domestic market price as determined by CCC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Export and barter programs for cotton are governed by other announcement references (NO-EX-28, CN-EX-22, NO-C-27, CN-EX-27) and specific terms there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-condition cotton and claim-establishing sales
rubrics_metrics.description: Cotton below grade or in special condition (Below Grade, Sample Loose, Damaged Pickings, etc.) will be offered periodically on the basis of samples representing the cotton for the purpose of establishing claims against producers and others according to schedules issued by CCC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcements NO-C-18 and NO-C-20 and periodic schedules govern these sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peanut restricted-use sale conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: When stocks are available, restricted-use sales of peanuts are governed by Announcement PR-1 and associated lot lists; shelled peanuts of less than U.S. No. 1 grade may be purchased for foreign or domestic crushing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lot lists and invitation to bids issued by designated peanut associations/organizations specify quantities, types, grades, and whether for restricted or unrestricted use.
